Asset-hungry power companies and rising costs for new projects are shrinking the pool of investment targets, energy bankers say

Private-equity firms have made billions in recent years investing in natural-gas-fired power plants, but these deals are now becoming harder to find.

More power companies are looking to acquire these assets to feed the energy demand from the artificial-intelligence boom, investment bankers say. This competition and the rising costs of building new projects mean private-equity firms have fewer opportunities to acquire natural-gas-fueled electricity generators.
